title: The Garden of the Ninefold Court Anew
premise: In the valley of Hollowmere, where wards have kept magic out for a century, Sable Pemberton makes her living as a memory-thief, extracting recollections from the wealthy and selling them to the desperate. When the border wards collapse on the night every star vanishes, she learns the truth: the valley was never a refuge but a prison, built to contain the Ninefold Court's exiled king, whose crown has been slowly devouring him. The stars went out because the Court's regent is harvesting them to complete the crown's thirteenth binding, which will make the king—or the thing wearing him—eternal. Sable, whose stolen memories include fragments of the king's own past hidden in her by her dying mother, must journey to the capital, ally with a disgraced court astronomer and a turncoat royal guard, and unbind the king before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. In the end, Sable sacrifices her own most precious memory—her mother's face—to shatter the crown, freeing the king and restoring the stars, though she chooses love over the throne he offers her.
about_author: Beatrix Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one claimed before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about small people entangled in large magics, and lives somewhere with too many clocks.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Sable extracts a dying matriarch's happiest memory for a grieving son, showing her craft and her rule: never keep what you steal. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism; she keeps one memory anyway—her mother's face—and we feel the crack beneath her control.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Bones
chapters.summary: Sable notices the valley's boundary stones humming wrong, and old-timer Mag the ferryman admits the wards were 'fed' something once a year—a ritual that stopped decades ago. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: creeping dread; the safety she resented may already be gone.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Every star goes out at once; the wards shatter like glass; riders bearing nine-pointed sigils enter the valley asking after 'the daughter of Lys.' POV: Sable. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo—the world she knew was a lie, and it has come to collect her.

chapters.title: What My Mother Left Me
chapters.summary: Searching her mother's hidden cache, Sable finds a locket-memory containing fragments of a king's childhood: a boy named Aldric, a garden, a coronation that felt like a funeral. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into purpose; she realizes she is carrying contraband royalty.

chapters.title: The Astronomer Who Counted Nothing
chapters.summary: Fleeing the riders, Sable collides with Wren Calloway, a disgraced court astronomer exiled for predicting the starless night. He explains the Thirteenth Binding: thirteen lunar turns to make the crown eternal. POV: alternating Sable/Wren. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Nine Roads Out of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: The riders burn the valley searching for Sable; Mag dies covering their escape, his last words: 'The king remembers being kind.' POV: Sable. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt hardening into resolve; the valley that caged her now bleeds for her.

chapters.title: A Court of Harvested Light
chapters.summary: First sight of the capital, Virelay, where captured starlight powers lamps and the poor sell memories to eat. Introduce the Regent Vessia, radiant and wrong-eyed. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: disillusionment; Wren sees how thoroughly the Court has corrupted wonder into currency.

chapters.title: The Guard Who Forgot His Oath
chapters.summary: Royal guard Captain Dain Ferros catches Sable thieving at a Court gala—but her stolen fragment of Aldric's memory triggers his own suppressed loyalty. He lets her go, then follows. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: shame and awakening; duty revealed as a leash.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns, Twelve Remaining
chapters.summary: Wren deciphers the Binding rite: each new moon, the crown devours a constellation. Eleven remain. They must reach the king before the twelfth. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: ticking-clock urgency; hope measured in arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath the Palace
chapters.summary: Dain leads them through forgotten passages to the sealed garden from Aldric's memories—alive, impossibly, fed on the king's fading self. There they find the king: hollow-eyed, half-consumed. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the tyrant they feared is a man being eaten alive.

chapters.title: Aldric Speaks in Fragments
chapters.summary: The king recognizes the locket-memory; playing it restores him briefly. He reveals Vessia forged the crown to bind him, and only a willing sacrifice of a treasured memory can crack it. POV: Aldric (first time). Emotional beat: fragile hope and dignity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Vessia's Generosity
chapters.summary: Vessia summons Sable openly, offering wealth and pardon if she surrenders the locket; she shows Sable visions of the chaos a free king might bring. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: temptation; power dressed as mercy, and Sable nearly believes it.

chapters.title: The Price of a Face
chapters.summary: Sable understands what the rite demands: her mother's face, her single kept treasure. She rehearses giving it up and cannot. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the book's thematic crux—love against duty made personal and unbearable.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Lantern District
chapters.summary: A trusted contact sells them out; Dain is captured covering the retreat; Wren's star-charts are seized. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: despair and cost; the plan lies in pieces and the twelfth new moon nears.

chapters.title: Twelve Becomes Eleven
chapters.summary: The crown devours another constellation publicly; the sky visibly empties; riots begin. In his cell, Dain refuses Vessia's offer to forget his oath-breaking. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: defiance in defeat; public grief becoming open rebellion.

chapters.title: The Memory Thieves' Guild Rises
chapters.summary: Sable calls in every debt across the city's underworld; thieves, smugglers, and memory-sellers—who all profit from human remembering—join her. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: solidarity; the invisible people of Virelay choosing to be seen.

chapters.title: Storming the Ninth Gate
chapters.summary: The assault on the palace during the pre-dawn dark; Wren reclaims his charts; Dain breaks free amid the chaos. POV: rotating trio. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by loss; victory purchased in blood.

chapters.title: The Crown Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Confronting Vessia, they learn the crown's true horror: it contains the memories of every king, and it offers Sable her mother's face back—real, whole—if she stops. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the final temptation; she almost takes the deal.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Under the penultimate new moon, Sable reaches the bound Aldric and gives up her mother's face willingly, cracking the crown's first seal as Vessia's rite falters. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: sacrifice fulfilled; grief and love fused into an act of will.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax: Aldric, restored enough to choose, renounces the crown rather than destroy it, letting its hoarded centuries of kings dissolve into returning starlight; Vessia, emptied of her borrowed radiance, is left mortal and small. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: catharsis; power relinquished, not seized.

chapters.title: Stars Returning, One by One
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the sky refills over weeks; Aldric abdicates to a council, offering Sable a place beside him; she chooses instead to return to a rebuilding Hollowmere—but not alone, and not to hide. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; love chosen freely over crowns offered.

chapters.title: The Garden of the Ninefold Court Anew
chapters.summary: Epilogue: a year later, Sable tends the palace garden-turned-school where children learn memory-craft ethically; she still cannot recall her mother's face, but she remembers everything her mother taught her. A letter arrives from Aldric. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: quiet peace; what is given away is not lost.
